texts.preamble: Pawan Kumar Maurya vs Parminder on 11 April, 2019 In The Court Of Ms. Savita Rao, Po, Mact (Ne), Karkardooma Courts, Delhi Mact No. : 465/2017 In The Matter Of : Pawan Kumar Maurya S/o Sh. Ram Kailash Maurya R/o House no. A6/166, ABlock Brijpuri, Delhi 110094 ........ Petitioner Vs. 1. Parminder S/o Sh. Ranbir Singh R/o Village Tiwala, The Charkhi Dabri District Bhwani, Haryana .........Driver 2. Ravinder S/o Sh. Mahinder Singh R/o Village & Po Jhanswa Distt. Jhajjar, Haryana ......Owner 3. The New India Assurance Company Limited Roii, 12/1, Jeewan Raksha Building, Aruna Asaf Ali Road, New Delhi - 110002 Mact No. : 465/2017 1/23 (Issuing Office : 353802 Near Sadar Police Station, Bahadurgarh, Haryana) .......Insurer Date of Institution of Petition : 09.11.2017 Date of Arguments : 27.02.2019 and 28.03.2019 Date of Award : 11.04.2019 Petition under Section 166 and 140 of M.V. Act, 1988 for grant of compensation Award 1.
texts.facts: This is claim petition filed by petitioner/claimant who met with an accident on 13.9.2017 at about 10.30 a.m at Toll Tax near Jathedi caused by Pawan Kumar Maurya vs Parminder on 11 April, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4903170/ 1 dumper/trailer bearing registration no. HR63C9867 (alleged offending vehicle). FACTS OF THE CASE 2. In terms of the contents of MACT petition, on 13.9.2017 at about 10.30 a.m., injured/petitioner was going on his motorcycle bearing no. DL - 5S BK 7477 towards his college from his residence alongwith his friends namely Saurav and Shivam who were sitting on the pillion seat of the motorcycle. When they reached at Toll Tax near Jathedi, suddenly a dumper/Trailer bearing registration no. HR 63C 9867 which was being driven by respondent no.1 in very high speed, rashly and negligently and in MACT No. : 465/2017 2/23 gross violation of traffic rules, came from behind and hit the motorcycle of petitioner with great force, due to which impact, petitioner fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries. Due to the accident, he suffered permanent disability. 3. FIR bearing no. 354/2017, u/s 279/337 IPC was registered at , P.S. Kundli, Distt. Sonepat, Haryana. The offending vehicle was found to be owned by respondent no. 2 and the said vehicle was insured with respondent no.3. 4. In Written statement filed on behalf of respondent no.1 and 2, it was submitted that no accident ever took place on the date of accident with the vehicle of respondents and FIR has been falsely registered against respondent no.1. as well as present petition has been filed with a view to harass and humiliate the respondents and to grab money . 5. In written statement filed on behalf of respondent no.3 i.e. Insurance Company, contract of indemnity was admitted, however, it was submitted that if at any stage during the proceedings, driving license was found to be not valid, then the insurance company would not be liable to pay compensation, if any. It was submitted that the alleged accident did not occur due to negligence on the part of respondent no.1 and rather it was the petitioner/injured who was not following the traffic rules because three persons are not allowed on motorcycle and due to this reason, motorcycle rider lost his balance and the motorcycle was slipped. It was further submitted that the petitioner has to implead the insurance company of his MACT No. : 465/2017 3/23 motorcycle bearing no. DL - 5S BK7477 for taking compensation because the accident was self driving accident. OPP. 3) Relief. 7. In order to establish his claim, petitioner examined himself as PW1 and Dr. Sumanth L, Sr. Resident from GTB Hospital was examined as PW2. In defence, no evidence was led by respondents . 8. Both the sides were directed to file their respective written submission in form VIB. Written submissions in form VIB were filed on behalf of petitioner as well as on behalf of respondent no.3 but no such submissions in form VIB have been filed on behalf of respondents no.1 & 2 till date. Having heard the arguments advanced by Ld. Counsel for the MACT No. : 465/2017 4/23 parties and having gone through the record, Issue wise findings are as under: ISSUE NO. 1 9. Injured/petitioner was examined as PW1 in the matter. He reiterated the contents of the petition in his affidavit of evidence regarding the accident having been caused due to rash and negligent driving by respondent no.1. After the accident, he was taken to hospital where he was given medical treatment and thereafter he was referred to Sant Parmanand Hospital where he remained admitted and was discharged on 9.10.2017. Due to the accident, he suffered 36% permanent disability of his right lower limb. 10. Based upon the complaint of injured/petitioner, FIR bearing no. 354/2017, u/s 279/337 IPC was registered at , P.S. Kundli, Distt. Sonepat, Haryana. Charge sheet has already been filed in the matter raising the accusing finger against the respondent no.1 i.e. driver of the offending vehicle. Though during the course of arguments, it was pointed out that in the charge sheet, owner of offending vehicle had been impleaded as accused, subsequent to which, clarification was sought from IO who appeared before the court and gave his statement/clarification on 28.3.2019 that pertaining to FIR no. 354/17 u/ 279/337/338 IPC, Parminder S/o Sh. Ranvir was named as an accused who caused the accident, whereas in charge sheet, inadvertently name of owner of offending vehicle i.e. MACT No. : 465/2017 5/23 Ravinder was mentioned which was a typing mistake and was corrected lateron. MLC of injured from Sant Parmanad Hospital where he was admitted on the date of accident, is on record, in terms of which, he had suffered injuries on his body including Open GradeIII Right Femur Shaft Fracture with Degloving Injury + Open Right MCL Injury with Capsular Damage and Cartilage loss. Pawan Kumar Maurya vs Parminder on 11 April, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4903170/ 3 11. The defence taken in written statement on behalf of respondents no.1 and 2 was that no accident ever took place with the offending vehicle allegedly driven by Respondent no.1. Police has charge sheeted respondent no.1 to face trial for offences punishable U/s 279/338/337 IPC arising out of abovestated FIR.
texts.arguments: At the same time, it was submitted that if the tribunal finds that petitioner is entitled to any amount of compensation, though not admitted, then the insurance company being the insurer of the vehicle is liable to indemnify the liability. It was incumbent upon Respondents no.1 and 2 to establish their defence on record by leading cogent evidence or to create dent in the testimony of PW1, in which they miserably failed. The testimony of PW1 thereby remained unrebutted and unimpeached on record with regard to the manner in which the accident was caused as well as with regard to the involvement of vehicle of respondent no.1 in the accident. 12. It was observed by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Bimla Devi and Ors. V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and Ors, (2009) 13 SC 530 that " the Tribunal has to borne in mind that strict proof of any accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be MACT No. : 465/2017 6/23 done by the claimant. The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied. " 13. Reliance is further placed upon Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Kamlesh, 2009 (3) AD (Delhi) 310, it was observed that " an adverse inference was drawn because the driver of the offending vehicle had not appeared in the witness box to corroborate his defence taken in the written statement. It was noted that there was nothing on record to show that the Claimant had any enmity with the driver of the offending vehicle so as to falsely implicate him in the case". 14. During investigation, driving license and RC of offending vehicle were obtained and necessary verification was conducted. Reliance is placed upon United India Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Deepak Goel & Ors., 2014 (2), T.A.C. 846 (Del.), wherein it was observed that " in a case, where FIR is lodged, chargesheet is filed, then the documents mentioned above are sufficient to establish the fact that the driver of the vehicle in question was negligent in causing the accident particularly when there was no defence available from his side". 15. Reliance is further placed upon 2009 ACJ 287, National Insurance MACT No. : 465/2017 7/23 Company Limited Vs. Pushpa Rana, wherein it was observed that " In case the petitioner files the certified copy of the criminal record or the criminal record showing the completion of the investigation by the police or the issuance of charge sheet under section 279/304 A IPC or the certified copy of the FIR or in addition the recovery memo and the mechanical inspection report of the offending vehicle, these documents are sufficient proof to reach to the conclusion that the driver was negligent. It was further held that the proceedings under the Motor Vehicles Act are not akin to the proceedings in a civil suit and hence strict rules of evidence are not required Pawan Kumar Maurya vs Parminder on 11 April, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4903170/ 4 to be followed in this regard". 16. It was submitted by Ld. Counsel for respondent no.3 that there was violation of the traffic rules, as Motorcycle is meant to be used by two persons, whereas there was triple riding on the motorcycle in the instant case, which is admitted fact on record, therefore it was the case of petitioner himself being negligent and in violation of the traffic rules. 17. No doubt, tripple riding on two wheeler, is in contravention to the provisions of motor vehicles act which casts duty on driver of two wheeler motor vehicle not to carry more than one person in addition to himself/herself on such vehicle. The appropriate punishment is provided for tripple riding on two wheeler u/s 128 r/w sec. 177 of the Act. Albeit, tripple riding by itself does not raise presumption that the person driving the motorcycle with two persons pillion riding is rash or negligent or his tripple riding contributes to the cause of accident since these provisions are made MACT No. : 465/2017 8/23 as safety measures for driver and pillion rider and breach thereof may amount to 'negligence' but such negligence will not amount to 'contributory negligence' on the part of pillion rider or 'composite negligence' on the part of driver of the motorcycle, unless such negligence was partly the immediate cause of the accident or damage suffered by the pillion rider. In other words, if the damage in the accident has not been caused partly on account of violation of Section 128 of M.V. Act by pillion rider of the motorcycle, the pillion rider is not guilty of contributory negligence and there would be no composite negligence on the part of its driver. Negligence on the part of deceased or the driver of the motorcycle, is to be established as a matter of fact which has not been done in the instant matter. Nothing has been brought on record to establish that it was because of the triple riding that the motorcycle lost the control and fell on the road and not because of the impact caused by offending vehicle. The argument raised by Ld. Counsel for respondent no.3, therefore, is rejected. 18. In the instant matter, Respondents no.1 & 2 having preferred not to lead any evidence in defence and they having failed to rebut the testimony of PW1 by creating dent in his testimony, unimpeached testimony of PW1 coupled with the other evidence as brought on record, apparently points out towards the accident having been caused by the driver of the offending vehicle i.e. respondent no.1 which was being driven in very high speed and had hit the petitioner/PW1 due to which he fell down on the road and sustained injuries. Hence, claimant /petitioner having been able to prove on MACT No. : 465/2017 9/23 the basis of preponderence of probabilities with regard to his having suffered injuries due to the accident having taken place on 13.9.2017 at Toll Tax near Jathedi, because of the negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle i.e. respondent no.1 herein, this issue is decided in favour of petitioner and against the respondents. As was noted in Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi Pawan Kumar Maurya vs Parminder on 11 April, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4903170/ 5 Transport Corporation 2009 (6) SCC 121, just compensation is pecuniary compensation which is fair and equitable, on the facts and circumstances of the case, to make good the loss suffered as a result of the wrong, as far as money can do so, by applying the well settled principles relating to award of compensation. It is not intended to be a bonanza, largesse or source of profit but at the same time cannot be the pittience. 20. Hon'ble Supreme Court in (2011) 1 SCC 343 titled Raj Kumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Anr. laid down the following general principles relating to compensation in injury cases: 4. The provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ( Act for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should , to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position MACT No. : 465/2017 10/23 prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. The court of tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. 5. The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following: Pecuniary damages ( Special Damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. 26. As noted in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Ors. Civil Appeal No. 8981/2010 arising out of SLP (C) No. 10383 of 2007, " where the claimant suffers a permanent disability as a result of injuries, the assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future earnings, would depend upon the effect and impact of such permanent disability on his earning capacity. Hon'ble Delhi High Court in the matter titled as " Vinod Kumar Bitoo Vs. Roshni & Ors." passed in appeal bearing no. MAC.APP 518/2010 decided on 05.07.12, has held as under: " It is difficult to measure the pain and suffering in terms of money which is suffered by a victim on account of serious injuries caused to him in a motor vehicle accident. Since the compensation is required to be paid for pain and suffering an attempt must be Pawan Kumar Maurya vs Parminder on 11 April, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4903170/ 9 made to award compensation which may have some objective relation with the pain and suffering underwent by the victim.
